correctness.rationale: Every one of the 27 cyclic trigrams is unique. A nine-mark 3-attractor must partition their 27 start indices into triples, uniquely forcing E={3,6,...,27}. For each of three residue classes the explicit table gives a cyclic bigram whose all occurrences miss E; this blocks all 27 cuts. The same E covers all trigrams and eight of nine bigrams at every cut; one extra position covers the last bigram. Any longer factor contains a uniquely occurring triple intersecting E, making ten a full attractor. The packaged standalone checker checks all 27 cuts and every length 1..29; the finite theorem is supported by exact symbolic combinatorics as well as exhaustive computation.

value.rationale: The problem explicitly asks whether each de Bruijn cycle can be unfolded to realize the tight factor-complexity attractor lower bound. This 27-symbol ternary example answers that yes/no question negatively while quantifying the exact extra cost of one mark for all rotations. The rotation-uniform obstruction is mathematically stronger than a counterexample for one unsuitable cut, and supplies a compact local witness table.
